sections.heading: What is a Computer?
sections.content:
A computer is an electronic device that accepts data as input, processes it according to a set of instructions (program), and produces output.

Key characteristics:
• Speed — processes millions of instructions per second
• Accuracy — produces error-free results
• Memory — stores large amounts of data
• Versatility — performs a wide range of tasks
• Diligence — works without fatigue

sections.heading: Components of a Computer
sections.content:
A computer system has five main components:

1. Input Unit — keyboards, mouse, scanner, microphone
2. Output Unit — monitor, printer, speakers
3. Central Processing Unit (CPU):
   • ALU (Arithmetic Logic Unit) — performs calculations and comparisons
   • CU (Control Unit) — controls sequence of operations
   • Registers — small, fast temporary storage inside CPU
4. Primary Memory — RAM (volatile) and ROM (non-volatile)
5. Secondary Storage — hard disk, SSD, pen drive, CD/DVD

sections.heading: Types of Memory
sections.content:
Primary Memory (Main Memory):
• RAM (Random Access Memory) — stores currently running programs and data; volatile (lost on power off)
• ROM (Read Only Memory) — stores BIOS/firmware; non-volatile
• Cache Memory — very fast memory between RAM and CPU

Secondary Memory:
• Hard Disk Drive (HDD) — magnetic storage, slower
• Solid State Drive (SSD) — flash memory, faster
• Pen Drive / Flash Drive — portable USB storage

Memory Hierarchy (fastest to slowest): Registers → Cache → RAM → HDD/SSD
